name: machine0
caveats: List prices; CPU sizes regular/shared, NVMe and dedicated premium differ. Marketing headline dedicated resources does not mean all vCPUs dedicated.
Monthly figures are illustrative, not a price cap; per-minute billing. $5 minimum refundable top-up. GPU bundle prices include CPU/RAM; do not treat them as GPU-only add-ons.
Suspending stops compute; image storage is $0.078/GB-month. Snapshot is disk-based unless memory preservation verified.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Bandwidth: $0.01/GiB beyond a "1-10 TB free allowance per size" (per-size split not published; card uses 1 TB). Machines are billed while running AND stopped; only suspend stops compute billing. No desktop/browser product: a GUI or headless browser must be installed by you on the VM.
Machines are auto-suspended when the prepaid balance drops to a suspension threshold (estimated snapshot/image/disk storage for the 7-day retention period), not at zero.

fleet.verification: First prepaid top-up unlocks paid concurrency; homepage minimum top-up $5. Additional ID/KYC not documented.
fleet.tiers: Free 1 until first top-up; new paid signups 50 concurrent since July 28, 2026. Existing accounts retain prior limits.
fleet.notes: Official changelog corrects old new-account cap of 3 to 50, while retaining free limit 1. 10/50 need first top-up; 300/1,000 higher quota procedure not stated. API request-rate increases are separate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: **Suspend** snapshots the VM, deletes the cloud instance, and stops machine billing.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: the suspend command (the snapshot 'suspended-<machine>-<date>-<time>' is taken automatically and restored on `machine0 start`), and automatic suspension when the prepaid balance hits the suspension threshold (changelog 1.0.166: 'Machines are auto-suspended when your balance drops to a suspension threshold'). Plain `stop` does not snapshot. No idle-timeout auto-suspend documented. Disk only (DigitalOcean-backed snapshot; VM gets a new IP, memory preservation not documented).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshot a VM into a reusable image. The VM is stopped automatically before snapshotting.
snapshot_on_demand.note: `machine0 images new <vm> <image>` (also MCP images tools); disk only, VM is stopped first (no live/memory snapshot). New machines boot from it (`machine0 new clone --image my-image`); images are versioned. $0.078/GB-month.

harness_api.quote: Gives agents the same capabilities as the CLI.
harness_api.note: API surface = CLI + remote MCP (machines, images, SSH keys, ssh_exec, sizes). Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode are preinstalled and profiles pre-authenticate them and serve prompts/MCPs, but you SSH in and run `claude` yourself; no API to start an agent with a prompt, stream its events or resume conversations.

ingress_rules.quote: HTTPS endpoints at `<vm>.mac0.io` are authenticated to the VM owner.
ingress_rules.note: Provider-side control is only the owner-authenticated HTTPS proxy (to port 80). The dedicated public IPv4 is filtered only by in-guest ufw (22/80/443 open by default), which is not provider-side; no cloud firewall / IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.quote: All VMs run `ufw` with ports 22, 80, and 443 open.
guest_firewall.note: Full DigitalOcean VM with sudo; ufw enabled by default, open more with `sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp`.

secret_proxy.quote: Injected credentials are plain files on the VM and travel with [snapshots](/platform/images).
secret_proxy.note: Profile secrets and integration credentials (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub, machine0 API key) are written into the VM as env files / credential files (/etc/environment, ~/.claude.json etc.); `--secret` only makes them write-only in the control plane. Profile MCP gateway proxies remote MCP servers (credentials held server-side), but that is MCP only, not HTTP egress injection.

volume_attach.quote: Disks are persistent block storage volumes that live independently of any VM.
volume_attach.note: 10-16384 GB, 5 per VM, 10 per account; attach at create or to a running VM; ~$0.1667/GB-month; not on GPU sizes or NixOS VMs yet.

volume_shared.quote: A disk lives in one region and attaches to one VM at a time.
volume_shared.note: Block volume, read-write, single attach. No shared filesystem documented.

anti_bot.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents. One command gives you (or your agent) an SSH-ready VM with dedicated CPU/RAM/GPUs, modern agents and tooling, a static IP, and HTTPS at <vm>.mac0.io.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — machine0 is a general-purpose persistent VM/compute product (card confirms browser: false, desktop: false), not a browser/stealth automation service.

captcha_solving.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser or CAPTCHA-solving product is offered; it is a bare VM platform.

egress_ip_type.quote: Every VM gets a dedicated public IPv4. Shown in machine0 get and machine0 ls.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard cloud-datacenter IPv4 (DigitalOcean-backed per card caveats), not residential/mobile.

fork_running.quote: Snapshot a VM into a reusable image. The VM is stopped automatically before snapshotting.
fork_running.note: Cloning (via images) requires the source VM to be stopped first; a running machine cannot be cloned without stopping it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Snapshot any VM into a reusable image: machine0 images new my-vm my-image / machine0 new clone --image my-image
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Fork/clone is a disk-based image snapshot (VM stopped first); no memory state is captured or restored, so cloned VMs boot fresh rather than resuming running processes.

wake_on_request.quote: Suspend snapshots the VM, deletes the cloud instance, and stops machine billing. ... Resume later with machine0 start
wake_on_request.note: Starting/resuming a stopped or suspended VM is always an explicit CLI/MCP action (machine0 start); no documented mechanism auto-wakes a machine when an inbound request/HTTPS hit arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: STOPPED ... Resources reserved. Still billed at full rate.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle-timeout auto-stop/suspend is documented. The only automatic suspension is balance-based (wallet dropping to the suspension threshold), not idle-based; stop/suspend otherwise require an explicit command.

live_resize.quote: update — Update a VM's name, default SSH username, or SSH client initial command.
live_resize.note: The only in-place update operation documented (machine0 update) covers name/ssh username/initial command, not CPU/RAM; changing size requires creating a new VM or restoring from an image at a different size.

own_agent_api.quote: A remote MCP server lets agents manage their own fleet: spin up a box for a build, snapshot it, tear it down.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — machine0's own API/MCP drives its VM fleet (create/manage/destroy machines, images, SSH), not a first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: Connect AI agents to machine0 using the Model Context Protocol. POST https://app.machine0.io/mcp ... Gives agents the same capabilities as the CLI.

lang_python.quote: Ubuntu pre-installed with Docker, Node, Python, Claude Code, and Codex.
lang_python.note: Default ubuntu-24-04-loaded image ships Python out of the box.

lang_node.quote: Ubuntu pre-installed with Docker, Node, Python, Claude Code, and Codex.
lang_node.note: Default ubuntu-24-04-loaded image ships Node.js out of the box.

egress_allowlist.quote: Firewall: All VMs run ufw with ports 22, 80, and 443 open. To open more: machine0 ssh my-vm "sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp"
egress_allowlist.note: The only firewalling documented is an in-guest ufw for inbound ports; no provider-side outbound allow/deny list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: All VMs run ufw with ports 22, 80, and 443 open.
egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side HTTP method/path-level egress rules are documented; only in-guest ufw port rules exist.

static_egress_ip.quote: Resume later with machine0 start — the VM gets a new IP.
static_egress_ip.note: The dedicated public IPv4 stays fixed while a VM is continuously running/stopped, but changes every time a suspended VM is resumed, so it is not a durable fixed egress IP across the machine's lifecycle.

windows.quote: NixOS or Ubuntu with tools pre-installed.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only NixOS and Ubuntu Linux images are offered; no Windows machine option.

macos.quote: NixOS or Ubuntu with tools pre-installed.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux-only VM images (NixOS/Ubuntu); no macOS offering.

arm64.quote: The `-nvme` sizes run on newer-generation CPUs with NVMe storage ... The `-premium` sizes are dedicated (not shared) vCPUs, the fastest single-thread performance we offer.
arm64.note: No ARM/Graviton-style size or image variant is listed anywhere in the sizes table or images list; all sizes are generic x86 vCPU/GPU offerings.

self_host.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — machine0 is a hosted cloud service with its own control plane/billing; only the guest OS images (NixOS/Ubuntu configs) are open source, not the platform itself, and there is no self-hosted control-plane option.

byoc.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents.
byoc.note: No option documented to deploy machine0's control plane into a customer's own cloud account; VMs run in machine0's own regions/datacenters.

open_source.quote: All images are open source: NixOS, Ubuntu.
open_source.note: Only the guest VM image definitions (Nix flakes / Ansible playbooks, e.g. github.com/fdmtl/machine0-nixos and machine0-ubuntu) are open source; the core machine0 platform/CLI/control-plane service itself is not stated to be open source.

sso.quote: machine0 VMs are single-user machines, but factor this in before running untrusted multi-user workloads on a profiled VM.
sso.note: No teams/organization or SAML/OIDC SSO feature is documented; the product is built around individual accounts and per-user API keys/profiles.

eu_data_residency.note: Customers can choose --region eu (Amsterdam) or uk (London) when creating a VM, keeping the machine and its data within the EU/UK.

max_session_h.quote: VMs stay on until you stop or suspend them, and everything is billed by the minute.
max_session_h.note: No maximum session length is imposed; a running VM continues indefinitely until the user stops/suspends it or the balance is exhausted.

desktop.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents. One command gives you (or your agent) an SSH-ready VM with dedicated CPU/RAM/GPUs, modern agents and tooling, a static IP, and HTTPS at <vm>.mac0.io.
desktop.note: Product is a bare SSH-accessible VM (NixOS/Ubuntu); the docs list SSH access, an in-browser SSH *terminal* (text shell, not a GUI desktop), snapshots, disks and profiles as the feature set. No VNC/GUI desktop, no desktop-streaming or remote-desktop feature is documented anywhere in the docs index (introduction, platform, cli, mcp, examples). A user would have to install and expose their own desktop environment on the VM, same as any generic VM host.

browser.quote: In-browser SSH terminal: one click from the web dashboard for VMs with a managed key — no local setup needed.
browser.note: The only browser-related feature is a web-dashboard SSH *terminal* for shell access, not a hosted/managed web browser or headless-browser-as-a-service for the VM. No product page, FAQ, or docs section offers a browser primitive; caveats already note a GUI/headless browser must be installed by the user.

computer_use.quote: Gives agents the same capabilities as the CLI.
computer_use.note: MCP/CLI surface is machine lifecycle, images, disks, SSH keys, and ssh_exec — no screen/mouse/keyboard control (computer-use) tool of any kind is documented across mcp/machines, mcp/images, mcp/keys, mcp/ssh, or mcp/sizes.

image_oci.quote:
Custom images

Snapshot any VM into a reusable image:

machine0 images new my-vm my-image
machine0 new clone --image my-image
image_oci.note: "Custom images" means snapshotting a machine0 VM you configured, not importing an external OCI/container image as the VM's base. System images are fixed NixOS/Ubuntu builds; Docker itself runs only as a workload inside the VM (docker_inside: true), confirmed separately by `machine0 ssh my-vm docker ps -a` / `docker run --gpus all ...` examples. No `--oci-image`/registry-pull option exists in the images or machines CLI reference.

nested_virt.quote: Where do VMs run? DigitalOcean infrastructure across five regions (New York, San Francisco, London, Amsterdam, Singapore).
nested_virt.note: machine0's own docs (security, networking, vm-management, provisioning, FAQ) never mention /dev/kvm, nested virtualization, or running VMs/emulators inside a machine0 VM. machine0 VMs run as guest VMs on DigitalOcean infrastructure; standard DigitalOcean droplets do not expose hardware virtualization extensions to the guest, so nested KVM is not available. Derived from the documented DigitalOcean-backed VM architecture, not an explicit machine0 statement.

soc2.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents. One command gives you (or your agent) an SSH-ready VM with dedicated CPU/RAM/GPUs, modern agents and tooling, a static IP, and HTTPS at <vm>.mac0.io.
soc2.note: No security/trust/compliance page, SOC 2 badge, or mention of SOC 2 exists anywhere in the docs index (introduction, platform, cli, mcp, examples), the marketing site, or the changelog. machine0 is a small early-stage (YC) VM provider with no published compliance program; treated as not currently SOC 2 attested.

hipaa.quote: machine0 provides persistent cloud VMs, designed for long-running agents. One command gives you (or your agent) an SSH-ready VM with dedicated CPU/RAM/GPUs, modern agents and tooling, a static IP, and HTTPS at <vm>.mac0.io.
hipaa.note: No mention of HIPAA, BAA, or healthcare-compliance offerings anywhere in the docs, marketing site, or changelog. Small early-stage VM provider with no published compliance program; treated as not HIPAA-eligible.
